parsedVerdict.reasoning: CancelOrderUseCase.execute does what an application-layer use case should do. It loads the aggregate through a domain repository interface and leaves the business rule to the domain method order.canBeCancelled(). It hands stock release to the domain service StockManager.releaseStock and maps the result to an application DTO (OrderDto). The file contains no persistence code, no transport or framework code (no HTTP, database or ORM calls), and no business rules written inline. The cancellation rule and the stock logic both stay in the domain. The method also never changes or saves the order's status, and it loads every product with findAll(). These may be correctness or performance problems, but they don't put a responsibility in the wrong layer.
